domain_label: Evidence Acquisition & Source Quality (Knowledge Acquisition subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
scope is the acquisition-and-grading method itself; the substantive answer to the question is out of scope and lives in the composed domain specialists
evidence labels are GRADE/CERQual-style claims about confidence in a body of evidence, not assertions of ground truth, and are always defeasible
candidate sources and the knowledge gaps (competency questions) are available as inputs to the method
exclusions: asserting domain conclusions or making decisions, professional advice, or recommendations
generating new domain knowledge rather than appraising existing sources
search/retrieval engineering and crawling infrastructure (assumed upstream)
ground-truth verification; the method grades confidence in evidence, not truth

competency_questions.question: For each knowledge gap, what evidence would close it and at what target tier, before any source is collected?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACQUISITION_PLAN defines the per-gap evidence requirement and target tier

competency_questions.question: How is each source typed as primary/secondary and empirical/testimonial, including mixed or interpretive sources?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOURCE_TYPING and PRIMARY_SECONDARY classify each source by epistemic type and resolve mixed sources

competency_questions.question: How are sources grouped by independence so corroboration is computed only across distinct groups?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INDEPENDENCE_GROUP partitions sources into independence groups

competency_questions.question: How is circular reporting detected so apparent breadth is not mistaken for independent corroboration?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CITATION_CHAIN traces chains to primaries and flags circularity over the independence groups

competency_questions.question: How is a claim triangulated across independent groups, and how are corroboration and contradiction tracked and kept visible?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRIANGULATION converges across groups; CORROBORATION logs support and keeps contradiction explicit

competency_questions.question: How is provenance recorded and how does the append-only ledger keep every judgment auditable and revisable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROVENANCE records origin/date/locator; SOURCE_LEDGER appends every judgment immutably

competency_questions.question: How are freshness and authority appraised without conflating recency or fame with reliability?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FRESHNESS keys recency to volatility; AUTHORITY weights domain-relevant expertise over prominence

competency_questions.question: How are source bias and conflicts of interest appraised and bounded so neither slant nor stake silently drives the grade?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOURCE_BIAS estimates distortion direction; CONFLICT_OF_INTEREST flags stakes and bounds tier lift

competency_questions.question: How are sampling/coverage bias and verifiability/reproducibility assessed for empirical sources?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SAMPLING_BIAS checks representativeness and coverage; REPRODUCIBILITY checks verifiability and replication

competency_questions.question: How are pivotal sources stress-tested for fabrication or coordinated disinformation without sliding into unfalsifiable rejection of all evidence?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RED_TEAM_SOURCE checks pivotal corroboration against a fabrication/coordinated-origin threat model and bounds skepticism

competency_questions.question: How is a GRADE-style evidence tier assigned to a claim from the full appraisal set?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GRADE_TIER applies the rubric with explicit upgrade/downgrade reasoning

competency_questions.question: How is evidence-label legality enforced so a 'high' label is impossible without >=2 distinct-independence-group sources?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVIDENCE_LABEL_LEGAL gates the tier against the distinct-group requirement; GRADE_TIER supplies the tier

competency_questions.question: How is a claim's confidence derived from its legal tier and kept defeasible as a claim about evidence, not a claim of truth?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONFIDENCE_DERIVE maps the legal tier to confidence qualified by contradictions and disclosed revision conditions

competency_questions.question: How is the cost of further acquisition accounted for and on what recorded basis does collection stop?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COST_OF_EVIDENCE costs the next source; STOPPING_RULE halts on legal-tier/saturation/cost conditions with a recorded basis

glossary.definition: a source reporting an original observation, study, measurement, or record at first hand
a source that describes, summarizes, or interprets one or more primary sources
a source whose claim rests on observation, measurement, or experiment rather than assertion
a source whose claim rests on assertion, opinion, or report rather than direct evidence
a set of sources sharing an origin, dataset, author cluster, or funder; corroboration counts only across distinct groups
apparent multi-source agreement that collapses to one origin because the sources all trace back to it
strengthening a claim by convergence of distinct independence groups, ideally using different methods
the recorded origin, authorship, date, and chain of custody of a source
an ordinal GRADE-style label (high/moderate/low/very_low) summarizing confidence in a body of evidence, not a truth value
the structural rule that a tier may be applied only if its preconditions hold (high requires >=2 distinct-group sources)
the point at which adding further independent sources no longer changes a claim's tier
a stated confidence that remains revisable under disclosed conditions and is a claim about evidence, not about truth

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for evidence-acquisition and source-quality work units, informed by GRADE evidence grading, library/source-evaluation rubrics (CRAAP), intelligence-analysis source-independence discipline, and systematic-review methodology; no supplied dataset
source_registry.citation_or_locator: GRADE Working Group: Guyatt et al. 2008 (BMJ, 'GRADE: an emerging consensus on rating quality of evidence'); Lewis & Wilson on source evaluation and the CRAAP test (California State University, Meriam Library) cf. Patrick Wilson 1983 'Second-Hand Knowledge: An Inquiry into Cognitive Authority'; Richards J. Heuer Jr. 1999 'Psychology of Intelligence Analysis' (source independence and circular reporting); Higgins & Green (eds.) Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions; Lewis & Clark / CERQual (Lewin et al. 2015) for qualitative-evidence confidence

nodes.definition: For each open knowledge gap (competency question), plan what evidence would close it: the claim to be supported, the kinds of sources that could bear on it, and the target evidence tier, before any source is collected.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a gap is added, retired, or its target evidence tier changes

pros.claim: A gap-driven plan makes acquisition purposeful and bounds search to what would actually change the answer
pros.example: planning that a dosage claim needs >=2 independent trials before collecting any source

cons.claim: Planning the desired evidence shape can bias collection toward confirming sources
cons.example: specifying 'find trials that show benefit' instead of 'find trials about the effect'

failure_modes: collecting sources with no target claim or tier
plan conflates the question with a preferred answer
acceptance_tests: every active gap has a target claim and a target evidence tier before collection begins

nodes.definition: Classify each candidate source by epistemic type: primary vs secondary, and empirical (observational/experimental/measured) vs testimonial (assertion/opinion/report), so its evidential weight is determined by what kind of thing it is.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the source-type taxonomy or empirical/testimonial boundary is revised

pros.claim: Typing each source up front lets downstream weighting and grading apply type-appropriate rules rather than treating all citations alike
pros.example: a peer-reviewed RCT and a tweet quoting it are not weighed the same once typed

cons.claim: Type labels can be gamed by presentation; a testimonial dressed as data can be mis-typed as empirical
cons.example: a marketing whitepaper formatted like a study

failure_modes: empirical claim backed only by testimonial source
secondary source mistaken for primary evidence
acceptance_tests: every collected source carries a resolved primary/secondary and empirical/testimonial type

nodes.definition: Maintain the primary/secondary distinction precisely: a primary source reports the original observation, study, or record; a secondary source describes, summarizes, or interprets primary sources. Resolve mixed sources to the part being cited.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the primary/secondary criteria are refined

pros.claim: Tracing to the primary source removes layers of interpretation and lets the original evidence be appraised directly
pros.example: a systematic review (secondary) is followed to the trials (primary) it pools

cons.claim: Primary is not automatically better: a flawed primary study can be worse than a careful secondary synthesis
cons.example: a single small biased trial vs a rigorous meta-analysis

failure_modes: citing a secondary summary as if it were the primary evidence
a review's framing inherited without checking the primaries
acceptance_tests: each cited claim is resolved to whether it rests on a primary or a secondary source

nodes.definition: Partition sources into independence groups: sources that ultimately derive from the same origin, dataset, author cluster, or funder share a group. Two sources corroborate only if they sit in DISTINCT independence groups.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the independence criteria or grouping policy changes

pros.claim: Grouping by independence is what makes corroboration meaningful: distinct groups give genuinely independent confirmation
pros.example: three outlets all reprinting one wire story collapse into one group, not three confirmations

cons.claim: Independence is a judgment call; over-splitting fakes independence, over-merging discards real corroboration
cons.example: treating two labs sharing a dataset as independent because the papers differ

failure_modes: counting common-source repeats as independent confirmation
merging genuinely independent sources into one group
acceptance_tests: every source is assigned an independence group, and corroboration is computed only across distinct groups
revisit_triggers: a hidden common source is discovered after grouping

nodes.definition: Trace each source's citation chain back toward primaries and detect circular reporting: where A cites B, B cites C, and C cites A (or all trace to one origin), so apparent breadth collapses to a single point.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the chain-tracing depth policy or circularity definition changes

pros.claim: Following citation chains exposes circular reporting that independence grouping alone can miss
pros.example: five 'independent' articles all footnote the same retracted study

cons.claim: Chains can be deep, ambiguous, or paywalled, so full tracing is sometimes impractical
cons.example: a claim's origin sits behind an unrecoverable internal report

failure_modes: circular reporting mistaken for corroboration
chain tracing abandoned, origin left unknown
acceptance_tests: every corroborating set is traced far enough to rule out a shared origin or an explicit circularity is flagged
revisit_triggers: a circular-reporting incident is found post-grade

nodes.definition: Triangulate a claim across independent groups and across source types: a claim gains strength when distinct independence groups, ideally using different methods, converge on it.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the triangulation rule or method-diversity policy changes

pros.claim: Convergence across independent groups using different methods is far stronger than repetition within one method
pros.example: a survey, an administrative record, and an experiment all pointing the same way

cons.claim: Triangulation can manufacture false confidence if the 'independent' methods share a hidden bias
cons.example: three methods all built on the same flawed sampling frame

failure_modes: calling within-group agreement triangulation
ignoring a divergent independent group
acceptance_tests: a claim's tier reflects convergence across distinct independence groups, not within-group repetition
revisit_triggers: a converged claim later contradicted by a missed group

nodes.definition: Track, per claim, which sources corroborate and which contradict it, with the contradiction left visible rather than averaged away, so that disagreement is an explicit signal feeding the tier.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the corroboration/contradiction accounting policy changes

pros.claim: Keeping contradictions explicit prevents premature consensus and forces the tier to reflect real disagreement
pros.example: two strong independent groups disagree, so the claim cannot be graded high

cons.claim: Counting sources for/against invites vote-counting that ignores quality differences
cons.example: five weak corroborations outvoting one strong contradiction

failure_modes: averaging away a credible contradiction
vote-counting sources instead of weighing them
acceptance_tests: every claim records both its corroborating and its contradicting sources, and unresolved contradiction caps the tier
revisit_triggers: a buried contradiction surfaces after grading

nodes.definition: Record the provenance of each source: who produced it, when, from what, through what chain of custody, so every judgment can be traced back to an identifiable origin.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the provenance schema or required fields change

pros.claim: Recorded provenance is the precondition for independence grouping, freshness, and later audit or revision
pros.example: a claim can be re-checked because its source, date, and access path were logged

cons.claim: Provenance capture adds overhead and is only as good as what the source discloses
cons.example: an anonymized leak with no verifiable origin

failure_modes: judgment recorded without a traceable source
provenance lost so revision is impossible
acceptance_tests: every source carries origin, date, and a retrieval locator sufficient to re-find and re-appraise it
revisit_triggers: a source cannot be re-located when re-checked

nodes.definition: Assess each source's recency relative to the claim's volatility: how quickly the underlying facts change and whether the source is current enough, while not discounting durable, well-established findings merely for being old.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the volatility model or freshness thresholds change

pros.claim: Freshness keyed to volatility flags stale sources on fast-moving claims without penalizing stable established knowledge
pros.example: a 2-year-old price is stale; a decades-old physical constant is not

cons.claim: Recency can be mistaken for reliability: the newest source is not automatically the most trustworthy
cons.example: a fresh preprint preferred over a replicated older study

failure_modes: stale source used for a volatile claim
durable finding discarded only for age
acceptance_tests: each source's recency is judged against the claim's volatility, with supersession flagged
revisit_triggers: a stale source is found to have driven a grade

nodes.definition: Weight a source by the relevant authority and expertise of its producer in the specific claim domain, distinguishing demonstrated domain competence from generic fame or credential transfer.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the authority rubric or domain-relevance criteria change

pros.claim: Weighting domain-relevant expertise keeps appraisal grounded in competence on the actual claim
pros.example: a virologist on a virology claim outweighs a celebrity endorsement

cons.claim: Authority weighting can become an appeal to authority that overrides independent corroboration
cons.example: deferring to one eminent expert against several independent contradicting sources

failure_modes: credential in one field transferred to an unrelated claim
fame counted as evidence
acceptance_tests: authority weight reflects expertise relevant to the specific claim, not generic prominence
revisit_triggers: a famous-source deference error is detected

nodes.definition: Appraise systematic bias in a source: framing, selection, ideological or commercial slant, and direction of likely distortion, separate from random error, so the bias direction is carried into grading.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the bias taxonomy or appraisal method changes

pros.claim: Naming the likely direction of bias lets corroboration across oppositely-biased independent groups be especially informative
pros.example: agreement between a pro- and an anti- aligned source is strong signal

cons.claim: Bias appraisal can itself be biased; an analyst may over-discount sources they disagree with
cons.example: dismissing a credible source as biased to protect a prior

failure_modes: bias unexamined so slant leaks into the grade
analyst's own bias drives the appraisal
acceptance_tests: each source carries a bias appraisal with an estimated direction of distortion
revisit_triggers: a slanted source is found to have skewed a grade

nodes.definition: Flag conflicts of interest: financial, institutional, or personal stakes the source's producer has in the claim's outcome, recorded as a provenance-linked flag that constrains how far the source can lift a tier.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the conflict-of-interest disclosure policy changes

pros.claim: An explicit COI flag prevents a stakeholder's self-serving evidence from silently inflating confidence
pros.example: a manufacturer-funded study of its own product is flagged before it lifts a tier

cons.claim: COI is a risk indicator, not a refutation; conflicted sources can still be correct
cons.example: over-discounting all industry research regardless of methodology

failure_modes: undisclosed conflict inflates a tier
conflicted source treated as automatically false
acceptance_tests: every source's known conflicts of interest are flagged and bounded in their tier influence
revisit_triggers: an undisclosed conflict is discovered after grading

nodes.definition: Assess sampling and coverage bias in empirical sources: whether the studied or measured population represents the claim's target population, and whether the search itself missed whole classes of evidence.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the sampling-appraisal or search-coverage policy changes

pros.claim: Checking representativeness and search coverage catches confident conclusions drawn from unrepresentative or selectively published evidence
pros.example: a benefit seen only in one demographic, or only in published positive trials

cons.claim: Perfect coverage is unattainable; over-strict representativeness can reject all available evidence
cons.example: demanding a globally representative sample for a local question

failure_modes: unrepresentative sample generalized to the target population
search omits a whole evidence class
acceptance_tests: each empirical source's representativeness and the search's coverage gaps are appraised
revisit_triggers: a coverage gap is found to have biased a conclusion

nodes.definition: Check whether a source's claim is verifiable or reproducible: whether the method, data, or record could in principle be re-run or re-inspected to reach the same finding, and whether independent replication exists.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the reproducibility / verifiability criteria change

pros.claim: Verifiability and replication are strong, hard-to-fake quality signals that a single confident assertion cannot match
pros.example: an effect that independently replicates outranks a charismatic one-off claim

cons.claim: Reproducibility evidence is often absent even for true claims, so its lack must not be read as falsity
cons.example: a sound field observation that cannot be re-run

failure_modes: unverifiable assertion graded as if confirmed
absence of replication read as disproof
acceptance_tests: each claim records whether it is verifiable and whether independent replication exists
revisit_triggers: a non-reproducible result is found to have anchored a grade

nodes.definition: Adversarially stress each pivotal source: could it be fabricated, planted, manipulated, or an artifact of a disinformation/astroturfing campaign engineered to look like independent corroboration?

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the threat model or disinformation indicators change

pros.claim: An adversarial pass catches engineered corroboration that ordinary appraisal, taking sources at face value, would accept
pros.example: a swarm of fake 'independent' reviews tracing to one operation

cons.claim: Adversarial skepticism can slide into unfalsifiable conspiracy that rejects all evidence
cons.example: dismissing every contrary source as a plant

failure_modes: coordinated disinformation accepted as independent corroboration
skepticism becomes unfalsifiable and rejects everything
acceptance_tests: each pivotal corroboration is checked against a fabrication / coordinated-origin threat model
revisit_triggers: an engineered-corroboration incident is found post-grade

nodes.definition: Assign a GRADE-style evidence tier (high / moderate / low / very_low) to each claim from the full appraisal: source types, independence, triangulation, corroboration/contradiction, freshness, authority, bias, COI, sampling, reproducibility, and the adversarial check.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the GRADE tier rubric or its inputs change

pros.claim: A single explicit tier, derived from many appraisal dimensions, gives a transparent, auditable confidence summary per claim
pros.example: a claim downgraded for inconsistency and upgraded for a large independent effect, with reasons logged

cons.claim: Compressing many dimensions into one ordinal tier loses nuance and invites disputes at the boundaries
cons.example: two analysts split between moderate and high on the same body of evidence

failure_modes: tier asserted without recorded reasons
tier read as a claim of truth rather than confidence in evidence
acceptance_tests: every graded claim carries a GRADE-style tier with explicit upgrade/downgrade justification
revisit_triggers: two analysts disagree on a tier for the same evidence body

nodes.definition: Enforce evidence-label legality: a tier may only be applied if its structural preconditions hold. A 'high' label REQUIRES a non-null claim plus >=2 sources in DISTINCT independence groups; 'moderate' requires >=1 source; weaker labels carry no source-count obligation. An illegal label is rejected, not downgraded silently.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the label-legality rule or its source-count thresholds change

pros.claim: A legality gate makes a strong label structurally impossible without genuine independent corroboration, closing the gap between a confident grade and the evidence backing it
pros.example: a 'high' with two same-origin sources is rejected as illegal before it can be recorded

cons.claim: Strict legality can block a defensible 'high' when only one strong source exists yet a decision is needed under thin evidence
cons.example: one definitive but lone audited record cannot earn 'high' under the rule

failure_modes: a high label recorded with sources sharing one independence group
gate bypassed under time pressure
acceptance_tests: no 'high' label exists unless backed by >=2 sources in distinct independence groups; every illegal label is rejected with a reason
revisit_triggers: an illegal label is found to have been recorded

nodes.definition: Account for the cost and effort of acquiring further evidence per gap: access, time, and analyst load, expressed as the marginal cost of the next source against its expected effect on the tier.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the cost model or access constraints change

pros.claim: Costing the next source against its expected tier impact keeps acquisition proportionate and feeds the stopping rule
pros.example: not paying for a tenth same-group source that cannot legally lift the tier

cons.claim: Optimizing for cost can starve a high-stakes claim of the corroboration it genuinely needs
cons.example: stopping cheaply on a safety-critical claim

failure_modes: effort spent on sources that cannot change the tier
cost pressure starves a critical claim
acceptance_tests: each gap tracks the marginal cost and expected tier impact of acquiring its next source
revisit_triggers: a critical claim was under-evidenced to save cost

nodes.definition: Decide when to stop acquiring evidence for a gap: stop when the target tier is reached and legal, when added independent sources stop changing the tier (saturation), or when marginal cost exceeds expected tier gain — recording WHY collection stopped.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the stopping-rule thresholds or saturation definition change

pros.claim: An explicit stopping rule prevents both premature closure and endless collection, and records the basis for stopping
pros.example: stop at saturation once a third independent group adds no tier change

cons.claim: Any stopping threshold can stop too early on a hard claim or too late on an easy one
cons.example: declaring saturation after two groups when a divergent third existed

failure_modes: stopping before the legal target tier is reached
collecting past saturation with no tier change
acceptance_tests: collection halts only on a recorded condition: legal target tier reached, saturation, or cost exceeding expected gain
revisit_triggers: a premature or runaway stop is found in audit

nodes.definition: Derive a claim's confidence as a function of its graded source set and the legality gate: confidence is the legal tier qualified by the live contradictions and disclosed revision conditions, never an assertion of truth.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the confidence-derivation mapping or revision-condition policy changes

pros.claim: Deriving confidence mechanically from the legal tier keeps the stated confidence and its evidential basis in lock-step and always defeasible
pros.example: 'moderate, revisable if the contradicting cohort study is corroborated' rather than a bare 'probably true'

cons.claim: A confidence number can be over-trusted as if it were a probability of truth rather than confidence in evidence
cons.example: a 'high' read as 'certainly correct'

failure_modes: confidence detached from the source set
confidence reported as truth, with no revision conditions
acceptance_tests: each claim's confidence is a recorded function of its legal tier, its contradictions, and explicit revision conditions
revisit_triggers: a claim's confidence diverged from its underlying source set

nodes.definition: Maintain an append-only ledger of every source, its type, independence group, provenance, all appraisals, the assigned tier, the legality decision, and the stopping basis — the single auditable record the whole method writes to and reads from.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the ledger schema or append-only / immutability policy changes

pros.claim: One append-only ledger makes every grade, legality decision, and stop reproducible and revisable without losing the prior record
pros.example: a downgrade appends a new entry citing a new contradiction, leaving the original judgment auditable

cons.claim: An append-only ledger grows without bound and needs disciplined indexing to stay usable
cons.example: thousands of source entries across many gaps

failure_modes: judgments overwritten so history is lost
ledger desynced from the actual appraisals
acceptance_tests: every source and every grade/legality/stop decision is appended immutably with enough provenance to re-audit
revisit_triggers: an in-place overwrite of a prior judgment is detected

edges.why_related: circular-reporting traces are a primary input to the disinformation threat model
a stop short of target tier feeds back to re-plan or re-scope the gap
a derived confidence below target reopens the gap for more acquisition
coverage gaps are where coordinated planted evidence most easily hides
a claim's volatility sets how quickly a stopped grade must be revisited
shared authoritative origins collapse otherwise-distinct-looking sources into one group
appended contradictions in the ledger trigger re-derivation of a claim's confidence
acquisition thoroughness pulls toward more sources while cost and the stopping rule pull toward halting
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: acquire to the legal target tier, then stop: when saturation or the cost-vs-gain bound is hit, halt even if more thoroughness is conceivable, recording the basis

edges.why_related: weighting a famous authority highly conflicts with the independence requirement that bars deferring to one source
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: never let authority weight substitute for independence: a single eminent source cannot satisfy the >=2-distinct-group requirement no matter how authoritative

edges.why_related: freshness pressure to prefer the newest source conflicts with the reliability of an older but well-replicated established source
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: key recency to volatility: prefer fresher sources only for volatile claims, and do not discount a replicated established finding merely for being older than a fresh un-replicated one

edges.why_related: strict high-label legality conflicts with the pressure to state a high confidence and answer when evidence is thin
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: hold the legality line: when independent corroboration is missing, cap the legal tier below high and report the lower defeasible confidence rather than relaxing the gate to answer under thin evidence

conflict_axes.name: thoroughness_vs_cost_and_stopping
conflict_axes.description: Acquiring more independent sources raises confidence but costs time and access; the stopping rule must halt before effort is wasted on sources that cannot change the tier.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: stop at the legal target tier or saturation; cost the next source against expected tier gain

conflict_axes.name: authority_weight_vs_independence
conflict_axes.description: Weighting an eminent source heavily can substitute deference to one famous voice for genuine independent corroboration.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: authority adjusts a source's weight but never satisfies the >=2-distinct-group requirement

conflict_axes.name: freshness_vs_established_reliability
conflict_axes.description: Preferring the newest source can displace an older but well-replicated established finding that remains more reliable.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: key freshness to claim volatility; do not discount replicated durable findings for age alone

conflict_axes.name: high_label_strictness_vs_answering_thin_evidence
conflict_axes.description: Strict high-label legality blocks confident labels without independent corroboration, which can leave a question answered only at a lower tier under time pressure.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the gate; report the lower legal tier with disclosed revision conditions rather than relaxing the rule

conflict_axes.name: corroboration_count_vs_quality_weighting
conflict_axes.description: Counting corroborating sources is simple but can vote-count weak sources over a strong contradiction.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: weigh sources by appraisal quality and independence, not raw count; unresolved contradiction caps the tier

conflict_axes.name: adversarial_skepticism_vs_usability
conflict_axes.description: A hard disinformation threat model catches engineered corroboration but, taken too far, becomes unfalsifiable and rejects all evidence.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply the red-team check to pivotal sources only and require a concrete fabrication mechanism, not mere suspicion

conflict_axes.name: early_typing_vs_collection_bias
conflict_axes.description: Specifying the desired evidence shape up front bounds search but can bias collection toward confirming sources.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: plan the evidence kind and tier, not the desired conclusion; keep the claim separate from a preferred answer

conflict_axes.name: provenance_completeness_vs_overhead
conflict_axes.description: Full provenance and an append-only ledger enable audit and revision but cost capture effort and unbounded growth.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: capture origin/date/locator and every decision; index and summarize rather than discard

conflict_axes.name: conflict_of_interest_flag_vs_dismissal
conflict_axes.description: Flagging a conflict of interest is a risk indicator, but treating conflicted sources as automatically false discards potentially correct evidence.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: bound a conflicted source's tier lift rather than excluding it; require independent corroboration to lift the tier

edge_cases.description: Three outlets all reprint one wire story and are counted as three independent confirmations.
edge_cases.trigger: sources sharing one origin assigned to distinct independence groups
edge_cases.mitigation: trace citation chains to the common origin and collapse the shared-origin sources into one group

edge_cases.description: A 'high' label is recorded with two sources that share a single independence group.
edge_cases.trigger: label-legality gate not enforced against the distinct-group requirement
edge_cases.mitigation: reject the label as illegal; require >=2 sources in distinct independence groups before allowing 'high'

edge_cases.description: A swarm of fabricated 'independent' reviews all trace to one coordinated operation and are taken as corroboration.
edge_cases.trigger: pivotal corroboration accepted without an adversarial origin check
edge_cases.mitigation: run the fabrication/coordinated-origin threat model on pivotal corroboration before it lifts a tier

edge_cases.description: An eminent expert's lone assertion is graded 'high' on the strength of their reputation.
edge_cases.trigger: authority weight allowed to satisfy the independence requirement
edge_cases.mitigation: authority adjusts weight only; a single source cannot earn 'high' regardless of authority

edge_cases.description: A credible contradicting study is averaged away so the claim reads as agreed.
edge_cases.trigger: contradiction merged into a net score instead of kept explicit
edge_cases.mitigation: keep contradictions explicit; unresolved contradiction caps the tier below high

edge_cases.description: A two-year-old figure is used for a fast-moving claim as if still current.
edge_cases.trigger: freshness not keyed to the claim's volatility
edge_cases.mitigation: estimate claim volatility and flag supersession; require a fresh source for volatile claims

edge_cases.description: A replicated decades-old established finding is discarded only for being older than a fresh un-replicated preprint.
edge_cases.mitigation: do not discount durable replicated findings for age; weigh replication over mere recency

edge_cases.description: A manufacturer-funded study of its own product silently lifts a claim to 'high'.
edge_cases.trigger: conflict of interest not flagged or not bounded in tier influence
edge_cases.mitigation: flag the conflict and bound its tier lift; require independent corroboration to reach 'high'

edge_cases.description: A benefit seen only in published positive trials is generalized as if the whole evidence base agreed.
edge_cases.trigger: publication/sampling bias and search-coverage gaps not appraised
edge_cases.mitigation: appraise representativeness and search coverage; consider unpublished and null results

edge_cases.description: An unverifiable one-off assertion is graded as if it were a confirmed result.
edge_cases.mitigation: record verifiability and replication status; treat the absence of either as a downgrade, not a disproof

edge_cases.description: Collection continues past saturation, paying for same-group sources that cannot legally change the tier.
edge_cases.trigger: stopping rule not applied; cost-vs-gain ignored
edge_cases.mitigation: detect saturation and stop when the next source cannot lift the legal tier

edge_cases.description: A claim's stated confidence is read as a probability of truth and a contradicting source later surfaces with no recorded revision path.
edge_cases.trigger: confidence detached from its source set and from disclosed revision conditions
edge_cases.mitigation: derive confidence from the legal tier with explicit revision conditions; append revisions to the ledger

workflow.description: For each open gap, fix the target claim, the source kinds that could bear on it, and the target evidence tier before collecting.
workflow.gate: every active gap has a target claim and target tier

workflow.description: Type each collected source as primary/secondary and empirical/testimonial.
workflow.gate: every source has a resolved type

workflow.description: Assign each source an independence group by origin, dataset, author cluster, and funder.
workflow.gate: every source is assigned an independence group

workflow.description: Trace chains toward primaries and flag circular reporting and shared origins.
workflow.gate: no corroborating set is left with an untraced shared origin

workflow.description: Triangulate across distinct groups and record corroboration and contradiction per claim.
workflow.gate: convergence is computed across distinct groups; contradictions logged

workflow.description: Record origin, author, date, and retrieval locator for every source.
workflow.gate: every source is re-locatable from its provenance

workflow.description: Appraise authority, freshness, bias, conflicts of interest, sampling, and reproducibility per source.
workflow.gate: each source carries the full appraisal set

workflow.description: Stress pivotal corroboration against a fabrication/coordinated-origin threat model.
workflow.gate: pivotal corroboration passes the threat model or is flagged

workflow.description: Assign a GRADE-style tier per claim with explicit upgrade/downgrade reasoning.
workflow.gate: every claim has a tier with recorded reasons

workflow.description: Reject any tier whose structural preconditions fail; 'high' needs >=2 distinct-group sources.
Derive defeasible confidence from the legal tier and stop on a recorded condition.
workflow.gate: confidence is derived and a stop basis is recorded

workflow.description: Append every source, appraisal, tier, legality decision, confidence, and stop basis immutably.
workflow.gate: the ledger contains an immutable, auditable entry for every judgment

priority_rationale: ACQUISITION_PLAN and SOURCE_TYPING are foundational; INDEPENDENCE_GROUP and CITATION_CHAIN establish the independence basis that makes corroboration meaningful; the appraisal layer (freshness, authority, bias, COI, sampling, reproducibility, red-team) feeds GRADE_TIER; EVIDENCE_LABEL_LEGAL gates the tier; CONFIDENCE_DERIVE, COST_OF_EVIDENCE and STOPPING_RULE close the method; SOURCE_LEDGER records everything.

dominance_rules.rule: A 'high' evidence label must never be recorded without >=2 sources in distinct independence groups
dominance_rules.rationale: high confidence requires genuine independent corroboration, not repetition of one origin
dominance_rules.trigger: a high label is proposed with sources sharing one independence group
dominance_rules.action: reject the label as illegal and cap at the highest legal tier

dominance_rules.rule: INDEPENDENCE_GROUP and CITATION_CHAIN must be settled before TRIANGULATION or the legality gate runs
dominance_rules.rationale: corroboration and the distinct-group count are only meaningful once independence and circularity are resolved
dominance_rules.trigger: triangulation or legality run on ungrouped or untraced sources
dominance_rules.action: block until grouping and chain tracing are complete

dominance_rules.rule: Authority weight may adjust a source's weight but must never substitute for the independence requirement
dominance_rules.rationale: deferring to one famous source is not independent corroboration
dominance_rules.trigger: a lone authoritative source proposed as sufficient for 'high'
dominance_rules.action: require a second distinct independence group regardless of authority

dominance_rules.rule: Unresolved credible contradiction caps a claim's tier below high
dominance_rules.rationale: genuine independent disagreement is incompatible with high confidence
dominance_rules.trigger: a credible contradicting source in a distinct group remains unresolved
dominance_rules.action: cap the tier and record the live contradiction

dominance_rules.rule: Conflicts of interest must be flagged before a conflicted source can lift a tier
dominance_rules.rationale: a stakeholder's self-serving evidence must not silently inflate confidence
dominance_rules.trigger: a conflicted source proposed as tier-lifting without a flag
dominance_rules.action: flag the conflict and require independent corroboration to lift the tier

dominance_rules.rule: Freshness must be keyed to claim volatility, not applied as a blanket preference for the newest source
dominance_rules.rationale: recency is not reliability; replicated durable findings should not be discounted for age
dominance_rules.trigger: a fresh un-replicated source preferred over a replicated established one on a stable claim
dominance_rules.action: weigh replication and volatility, not recency alone

dominance_rules.rule: Pivotal corroboration must pass the adversarial origin check before lifting a tier
dominance_rules.trigger: a pivotal corroboration would lift a tier without a red-team pass

dominance_rules.rule: Acquisition must stop on a recorded condition (legal target tier, saturation, or cost-exceeds-gain), never silently
dominance_rules.rationale: both premature closure and endless collection are failures; the basis must be auditable
dominance_rules.trigger: collection halts or continues with no recorded stop basis
dominance_rules.action: record the stop condition or continue to the legal target tier

dominance_rules.rule: Every grade, legality decision, confidence, and stop basis must be appended to the ledger immutably
dominance_rules.rationale: reproducibility and revision require an auditable, non-overwritten record
dominance_rules.trigger: a prior judgment overwritten in place
dominance_rules.action: append a new entry citing the change rather than mutating the old one

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not grade or label before sources are grouped by independence and chains are traced; regrading after a shared origin surfaces is wasteful
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-grading every claim after circular reporting is discovered late

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not propose a 'high' label without confirming >=2 distinct independence groups first; a rejected illegal label discards the grading work
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding a grade after the legality gate rejects an illegal high label

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not record judgments without provenance; retrofitting origin and date for audit requires re-collecting sources
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-collection when a judgment cannot be traced to its source

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not defer the conflict-of-interest and bias appraisal to grading time; a late COI flag can invalidate an already-recorded tier
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-grading after a conflict surfaces post-tier

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not skip the adversarial check on pivotal corroboration; discovering engineered corroboration after grading forces a full re-appraisal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-appraising a claim after planted evidence is found post-grade

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not collect past saturation; sources that cannot change the legal tier add cost without value
anti_rework_rules.prevents: wasted acquisition on tier-neutral same-group sources

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not detach confidence from the source set; a confidence stated without revision conditions must be re-derived when evidence changes
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing the basis for a confidence when a contradiction appears

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not overwrite prior ledger judgments; reconstructing lost history to explain a grade requires re-running the appraisal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-running appraisals to recover an overwritten judgment trail

iteration_protocol.trigger: circular reporting or a shared origin is discovered after grading
iteration_protocol.action: re-trace chains in CITATION_CHAIN, re-cluster in INDEPENDENCE_GROUP, and re-run the legality gate for affected claims

iteration_protocol.trigger: an illegal 'high' label is found in the ledger
iteration_protocol.action: reject and cap it via EVIDENCE_LABEL_LEGAL and append the correction in SOURCE_LEDGER

iteration_protocol.trigger: engineered or coordinated corroboration is detected post-grade
iteration_protocol.action: re-run RED_TEAM_SOURCE on pivotal sources and re-grade the affected claims

iteration_protocol.trigger: a credible contradiction surfaces in a distinct independence group
iteration_protocol.action: record it in CORROBORATION, cap the tier, and re-derive confidence

iteration_protocol.trigger: an undisclosed conflict of interest is discovered for a tier-lifting source
iteration_protocol.action: flag it in CONFLICT_OF_INTEREST, bound its influence, and re-grade

iteration_protocol.trigger: a graded claim's underlying facts have plausibly changed (volatility window elapsed)
iteration_protocol.action: re-assess recency in FRESHNESS and re-open the gap via STOPPING_RULE if the tier may have shifted

iteration_protocol.trigger: a search-coverage gap or sampling bias is found after grading
iteration_protocol.action: re-appraise representativeness in SAMPLING_BIAS and re-grade if coverage changed the evidence base

iteration_protocol.trigger: acquisition cost is overrunning with no tier change
iteration_protocol.action: recompute marginal cost-vs-gain in COST_OF_EVIDENCE and apply the saturation stop in STOPPING_RULE
